name: Oligoastrocytic Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of mixed neoplastic cells showing both astrocytic and oligodendroglial differentiation on histological examination
Immunohistochemical staining positive for GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) and OLIG2 markers
Detection of combined 1p/19q codeletion absence and IDH1/IDH2 mutation status to differentiate from pure oligodendrogliomas or astrocytomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological evidence of mixed astrocytic and oligodendroglial tumor cells with supportive immunohistochemical and molecular genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular classification has reduced the frequency of oligoastrocytoma diagnosis; integrated diagnosis using histology and genetics is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits corresponding to tumor location

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: feeling sick from increased brain pressure

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion
brain fluid buildup from tumor blockage
water accumulation in brain due to tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI showing mixed solid and cystic mass with heterogeneous contrast enhancement
T2-weighted hyperintense lesion with ill-defined margins in cerebral hemispheres
genetic: Absence of 1p/19q codeletion differentiates from pure oligodendroglioma
other: Histopathology demonstrating mixed astrocytic and oligodendroglial features
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and OLIG2

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly astrocytic cell population without oligodendroglial components
IDH mutation status and absence of 1p/19q codeletion
Uniform oligodendroglial morphology without astrocytic features
High-grade features with necrosis and microvascular proliferation
Rapid clinical progression and poor prognosis

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Wesseling P, Capper D. WHO 2016 Classification of gliomas. Neuropathol Appl Neurobiol. 2018.
